bugs.summary: Error for match.arg(<non-string>, ...) is not very illustrative
bugs.creator: michaelchirico4

comments.creator: michaelchirico4
comments.text:
Created attachment 3800
Handle wrong input type the same as any other in match.arg

```
match.arg(TRUE, c('a', 'b', 'c'))
# Error in match.arg(TRUE, c("a", "b", "c")) : 
#   'arg' must be NULL or a character vector
```

This message is typically seen by a user mis-using a function with an enum-ish argument, so I see two problems here:

 1. It implies a _vector_ is accepted (which is true only for `isTRUE(several.ok) || startsWith(several.ok, "all")`)
 2. It suggests that _any_ character vector will do, when in fact there are only 3 valid values.

I think it would be better to just show the "normal" `match.arg()` error here:

```
match.arg('d', c('a', 'b', 'c'))
# Error in match.arg("d", c("a", "b", "c")) : 
#   'arg' should be one of "a", "b", "c"
```

(also a nit: the first error uses "must" while the second uses "should")

(of course, enough familiarity with Go has me also wondering if this should obey the want/got approach more and report what was received in addition to what is expected: https://pkg.go.dev/testing)

----

In filing this bug I saw another deficiency in the case of `several.ok`:

```
match.arg(letters, c('a', 'b'), several.ok='all')
# Error in match.arg(letters, c("a", "b"), several.ok = "all") : 
#   'arg' should be one of "a", "b"
```

This is also a bit misleading -- `letters` _does_ have `"a"` and `"b"`; what's wrong is that there are _some_ mismatched inputs. The error could reflect that; I have elected not to pursue that nuance in the initial patch here.

I _have_ elected to retain the `NULL or` clarification in the updated error, which might not be desirable (e.g. I presume it will break a number of CRAN packages assuming base error messages are highly predictable: https://github.com/search?q=org%3Acran+%2F%27arg%27+should+be+one+of+%2F+path%3Atests&type=code).

comments.creator: maechler
comments.text:
Well, given that in so many places people grep for the error message,
such a change would cost quite a bit of human time fixing all these instances.

Also, note that  `"a"`  _is_ a character vector length one,
so "character vector" is correct.
If we'd write the function from scratch today, I'd simply use "character" instead 
(as all "character" are atomic vector, even if of length 0 or 1, see above),
but given the human time above, I don't think we should change it now.

Also (your '2.') the "suggestion" of _any_ character vector is really not true,
in the context of R (or programming in general, outside of language processing).
It is typical notably for this function that not every string / character vector will match, and given that an error is a desired outcome for non-matching input,

I propose to close this with something as 'WORKSFORME' or 'WONTFIX'.

comments.creator: michaelchirico4
comments.text:
I just want to make sure my intent here is understood. I don't mean to argue that "character vector" is incorrect, rather that it could be more helpful.

A more minimal change would be to just edit "character vector" to "character string" in the `isFALSE(several.ok)` case, for example.

We could also simply omit the 'or NULL' part from the error message in the patch; this would still lead to some CRAN churn, but less [1].

I don't think we should be _too_ beholden to what CRAN authors mistakenly (IMHO [2] [3]) hard-code in their test suites if we can substantially improve the R user experience. The proposed error is self-documenting -- the user immediately sees how to proceed.

[1] E.g. https://github.com/search?q=org%3Acran+%2Fmust+be+NULL+or+a+character%2F+path%3Atest+-path%3A_snaps&type=code. I'm of course happy to quantify this more formally if requested.

[2] data.table, for example, takes great pains to _only_ test error messages _under its control_: https://github.com/Rdatatable/data.table/blob/e26cf1b6b95474d90d3db462409e2d59e371b740/inst/tests/tests.Rraw#L200-L225

[3] I myself have just this month had to update a CRAN package because of a change to R's own messages, a fragility of my own making: https://github.com/r-lib/bit64/commit/b4f08213072de64f9b0448582290605ce7f4ab01
